sal_bw.text: Theorem 2.3 (Bernstein-Widder). f in CM if and only if there is a unique positive Radon measure mu on [0, infinity) such that f(x) = integral over [0,infinity) of e^(-xt) dmu(t).

sal_defs.source: D. S. Salazar, Bernstein Functions at Work: Coalescents, Copulas, and Subordination
sal_defs.text: Definition 2.1 (Completely monotone, Bernstein, and Stieltjes classes). Let all functions below be defined on (0, infinity) and take values in [0, infinity). (i) A function f is completely monotone, written f in CM, if f in C^infinity and (-1)^n f^(n)(x) >= 0 for every n >= 0 and x > 0. ... (ii) A function g is a Bernstein function, written g in BF, if g in C^infinity and g' in CM.

sal_subord.text: This dictionary - Bernstein-Widder for CM functions, Levy-Khintchine for Bernstein functions, and Bochner subordination for their composition - turns many analytic questions into statements about a representing measure that one can often write down explicitly [31, 19]. (Reference [31] there is R. L. Schilling, R. Song, Z. Vondracek, Bernstein Functions: Theory and Applications, 2nd ed., de Gruyter, 2012; the statement that a completely monotone function composed with a Bernstein function is completely monotone is NOT quoted there and its theorem number in [31] was not verified by us.)
